WORKING → WAITING · TASK → IDLE in a real OpenCode 2 session (everything that is not the plugin is blurred)

# @arandevcode/opencode-thinking > 🇪🇸 Also available in [Spanish](README-es.md) > 🔁 Want this on Claude Code? See [glow-thinking](https://github.com/arandevcode/claude-mods/tree/main/glow-thinking). A status band above the prompt and a state line in the sidebar that tell you, at a glance, whether OpenCode is busy, waiting on background work, or done. On OpenCode 2 the sidebar is framed too. **WORKING includes every subagent**, foreground or background. No config needed. Works on OpenCode 1.x and OpenCode 2. Runs locally, no telemetry, no network.

🐟

“Quien quiera peces que se moje el culo”
“If you want fish, get your ass wet”

— for my father, who taught me to roll up my sleeves and get it done

## States | Band | Color | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `WORKING` | rotating theme colors | The main turn **or any subagent** is running, in the foreground or in the background. | | `WAITING · TASK` / `WAITING · 2 TASKS` | amber | The turn is over but a background shell is still alive (OpenCode 2 only). | | `IDLE` | green | Nothing running and nothing pending. | OpenCode 1.x does not expose a reliable background-shell signal to TUI plugins, so there the band goes straight from `WORKING` to `IDLE`; `WAITING` is not simulated. Monitors and scheduled wakeups are Claude Code concepts with no equivalent here. When a background task finishes in OpenCode 2 it wakes the session with a new turn, so the band goes back to `WORKING` and then to `IDLE`.

## Install One package for both OpenCode generations: it ships an entry for each and loads the right one. ### OpenCode 1.x ```sh opencode plugin --global --force @arandevcode/opencode-thinking ``` Or install from GitHub source to follow latest development: ```json // ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json { "plugin": [ "https://github.com/arandevcode/opencode-plugins/tree/main/opencode-thinking" ] } ``` ### OpenCode 2 ```sh opencode plugin add @arandevcode/opencode-thinking ``` On OpenCode 2 the plugin command is `plugin add` (not `plugin --global`). Please [open an issue](https://github.com/arandevcode/opencode-plugins/issues) if something looks wrong. ### Compatibility | Feature | OpenCode 1.x | OpenCode 2 | |---|---|---| | WORKING with main turn + subagents (foreground and background) | ✅ | ✅ | | `WAITING · TASK` for a live background shell | ❌ no reliable plugin signal | ✅ | | `WAITING · MONITOR` / `SCHEDULE` | ❌ no equivalent | ❌ no equivalent | | Prompt border + state band | ✅ | ❌ full-width bar above the composer | | Sidebar state | ✅ | ✅ | | Border around the whole sidebar | ❌ | ✅ when the sidebar is visible | | `/thinking_visual` command | ✅ | ✅ | On very narrow terminals OpenCode hides the sidebar; there is nothing to frame, so the border is absent there. ## Updating Update the package with the command for your generation: ```sh # OpenCode 1.x opencode plugin --global --force @arandevcode/opencode-thinking@latest # OpenCode 2 opencode plugin update @arandevcode/opencode-thinking ``` On OpenCode 2, `plugin add ...@latest` is not an update command: when the package is already configured, it appends a second entry and OpenCode loads both copies ([anomalyco/opencode#56217](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/56217)). Use `plugin update` instead. If you already have a duplicate, remove the extra entry with `opencode plugin remove `. Then **restart the session**: a loaded plugin is not replaced in a running session. Reloading the window or the configuration is not enough. If the plugin is installed in more than one scope (for example the user scope and a project), update each one. If you installed from GitHub source or a local checkout, update that source instead. ## Uninstall **OpenCode 2:** run `opencode plugin remove @arandevcode/opencode-thinking`, then do the optional clean-up steps below. **OpenCode 1.x:** Three steps, in order: 1. Remove the plugin entry from your OpenCode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`): ```jsonc // delete the @arandevcode/opencode-thinking lines inside "plugin": [] { "plugin": [ "@arandevcode/opencode-thinking/tui", // ← remove "@arandevcode/opencode-thinking/server" // ← remove ] } ``` 2. Delete the shared state file the plugin uses for TUI ↔ Server IPC: ```sh rm -f ~/.config/opencode/thinking-visual-state.json rm -f ~/.config/opencode/thinking-visual-debug.log ``` 3. (Optional) Remove any local source clone you may have used to follow development: ```sh rm -rf ./opencode-thinking ``` Restart OpenCode and the status band, border and sidebar state will be gone. ## Commands | Command | Effect | |---|---| | `/thinking_visual` | Toggle all effects | | `/thinking_visual a` | Border animation only | | `/thinking_visual b` | Sidebar state only | | `/thinking_visual all` | Both | | `/thinking_visual none` | Disable | ## More Information ### How the state is calculated The plugin watches only the **focused conversation's session tree**. Sessions from another conversation, even if they are running at the same time, never affect the band. - **OpenCode 1.x:** listens to `session.status` and `session.idle` for every session and builds the parent/child map from `parentID`. When a conversation is focused, it walks the tree with `session.children()` so nested subagents are included. Only `busy`/`retry` sessions count as running. - **OpenCode 2:** reads the session status store, the session family and the running shell list. Every shell still alive in the focused tree counts as a pending task. Subagents are ordinary child sessions in both versions, so foreground and background subagents use the same rule: **any running descendant means WORKING**. Leaving `WORKING` has a small **400 ms settle window**. A foreground subagent can stop a few milliseconds before its parent resumes, and a completed background task wakes the session with a new turn; the window keeps the band from flashing `IDLE`/`WAITING` in those gaps. Entering `WORKING` is immediate. ### Project structure ``` ├── src/ │ ├── index.ts ← package entry │ ├── tui.tsx ← TUI plugin: band, prompt border, sidebar, keymap │ ├── v2.ts ← OpenCode 2 context adapter + background-shell snapshot │ ├── state.ts ← shared tree/state machine (WORKING > WAITING > IDLE) │ ├── server.ts ← v1 server plugin: /thinking_visual command │ └── types.ts ← shared config types and state-file path ├── tests/ ← state machine, v1 TUI and v2 adapter tests ├── docs/ │ └── ARCHITECTURE.md ├── images/ ├── example.opencode.json └── package.json ``` ### Install in another project ```jsonc // .opencode/opencode.json { "plugin": [ "@arandevcode/opencode-thinking/tui", "@arandevcode/opencode-thinking/server" ] } ``` ### Development ```sh npm install # install deps (type-check only) npm run build # compile src/ → dist/ npm test # build + state, v1 and v2 tests npm run dev # continuous compilation ``` ## TUI Patterns & Theme Colors are sourced live from `api.theme.current`, not hardcoded. The plugin also watches the theme signature (250ms polling) so theme changes mid-session are picked up by the next re-render. | State | Border + badge color | Badge text | |---|---|---| | **Working** | cycles `theme.primary` → `theme.accent` → `theme.success` → `theme.error` every 250ms | `WORKING` | | **Waiting** | solid `theme.warning` | `WAITING · TASK` / `WAITING · 2 TASKS` | | **Idle** | solid `theme.success` | `IDLE` | `theme.warning` is deliberately excluded from the WORKING rotation: amber is reserved for `WAITING`, so a pending background task cannot be confused with the animated working state. The same color drives the sidebar state, and on OpenCode 2 the sidebar border while visual mode `b` is enabled. This pattern follows the `opentui-theme-colors` convention: semantic theme keys (`primary` / `accent` / `success` / `warning` / `error`) instead of hardcoded palette values, and `themeSignature()` + `setInterval` polling for reactive theme changes. ## License MIT

# Changelog

## 0.5.0 — 2026-11-12
- Change: on OpenCode 2 the status badge now lives in the host prompt's additive right slot and the sidebar status sits above the host footer, so OpenCode 2 keeps its own location and version lines and the plugin never owns (or duplicates) the prompt. It coexists with other TUI plugins that render a composer.
- Fix: keymap commands use `name`/`category` instead of `id`/`group`.
- Change: the OpenCode 1.x composer border wraps the host prompt in a stable bordered box, so toggling it never remounts the prompt.

## 0.4.0 — 2026-11-10
- Fix: the band stayed on `IDLE` while subagents were running. `WORKING` now covers the main turn **and every subagent**, foreground or background, nested at any depth.
- New: `WAITING · TASK` / `WAITING · 2 TASKS` in amber on OpenCode 2 when the turn is over but a background shell is still alive. OpenCode 1.x has no reliable plugin-facing signal for this, so it goes `WORKING` → `IDLE` there.
- New: focused-conversation tree tracking. Sessions from another conversation no longer influence the band; this replaces the 0.3.2 rule that ignored all subagents.
- New: 400 ms settle window when leaving `WORKING`, so a foreground subagent handoff or a background task waking its parent never flashes `IDLE`/`WAITING`.
- Change: `WORKING` cycles `theme.primary` → `theme.accent` → `theme.success` → `theme.error`; `WAITING` is solid `theme.warning` and `IDLE` is solid `theme.success`. Warning is reserved for waiting so it cannot be confused with the working animation.
- Change: a shared state machine (`src/state.ts`) now computes the state for both OpenCode generations, with v1 event/tree and v2 store/shell adapters.
- Fix: the OpenCode 2 sidebar border now finds the right-anchored pane at any width, keeps its decoration through transient reflows, and no longer flickers or changes the root padding. Narrow terminals hide the sidebar, so there is nothing to frame.
- Docs: new states table, compatibility details, update instructions and simulated screenshots/GIFs with made-up data.

## 0.3.2 — 2026-11-06
- Fix: on OpenCode 2 the WORKING/IDLE indicator stayed on IDLE while the model was running. The TUI event listener receives `{ details }` and the adapter read `event.type` from the wrapper, so `session.execution.started` never matched. The adapter now unwraps the envelope (and still accepts unwrapped events).
- Fix: treat `session.execution.interrupted` as idle, alongside `succeeded` and `failed`.
- Fix: no more stray empty bordered box above the prompt on OpenCode 2, where the prompt element is not available.
- Fix: the spinner and color animation stayed frozen on OpenCode 2. The TUI entry was pre-compiled by tsc, which removes Solid's reactive JSX transform; it now ships as `dist/tui.tsx` and is compiled by the host runtime, so signals update live.
- Fix: the indicator no longer reacts to other sessions or subagents running in the background; it follows only the focused session and syncs when you switch.
- Change: on OpenCode 2 the indicator is now a full-width bar with a colored top border above the composer (`session.composer.top`), since the prompt itself cannot be wrapped.
- Change: the sidebar title box was removed. `WORKING`/`IDLE` now sits at the bottom of the sidebar, above the `cwd:branch` line (`before: sidebar.footer`).
- Change: the whole sidebar is framed with a heavy border; the sidebar is widened by the border width so its content (quota percentages, etc.) is not clipped, and the frame is kept clear of the terminal's clipped right edge.

## 0.3.0 — 2026-11-06
- OpenCode 2 support (early preview): the package now registers on both OpenCode 1.x and 2.x; tested on 2.1.2.
- Fix installation from npm on OpenCode 1.x and 2: accept current `@opentui` versions (0.4 to 0.x). Before this, `opencode plugin` failed with "unable to resolve dependency tree".
- README: separate install and uninstall steps for OpenCode 1.x and OpenCode 2, plus a compatibility table.
- Fix: Esc did not interrupt a running session (issue #1). The prompt was re-created on every animation tick, resetting its focus and the "esc again to interrupt" state; it is now created once.

## 0.2.2 — 2026-08-06
- Allow OpenTUI 0.5 peer dependencies.

## 0.2.1 — 2026-08-05
- Packaging cleanup: removed stray files from the published package.

## 0.2.0 — 2026-08-05
- Colors follow the active OpenCode theme; error boundary and guarded event handlers.

## 0.1.x — 2026-06
- First releases: animated rainbow border and sidebar glow while the model is thinking, plus IDLE state.
